findings.problem: TelemetryWorkflow uses ad-hoc booleans and a string status instead of an explicit typestate enum governing lifecycle transitions (e.g. Pending -> Validated -> Sent). Any ordering of field mutations is allowed, so invalid state combinations like is_sent=true with status!="sent" are representable.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct TelemetryWorkflow with is_validated=false, is_sent=true, and status="pending" simultaneously, violating the intended workflow invariant and producing silent telemetry corruption.
findings.fix: Define an enum TelemetryState { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } } and replace status, is_validated, is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms with a single state: TelemetryState field. Constructor enforces valid transitions only.

findings.problem: status: String is a raw primitive domain field that permits arbitrary string values ("sent", "SENT", "", "pending", "foobar"). This breaks pattern matching, makes state validation runtime-dependent, and hides illegal states.
findings.failure_mode: A caller sets status to an unhandled value, causing downstream match branches to fall through to defaults or log silently incorrect telemetry status.
findings.fix: Replace `status: String` with `state: TelemetryState` enum. If a display name is needed for external interfaces, derive it from the enum variant in the shell boundary.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are lifecycle booleans that can be independently toggled. This allows illegal combinations like is_validated=false, is_sent=true, or is_validated=true, is_sent=false with status="sent". The two booleans encode a 4-state truth table but only 3 are valid.
findings.failure_mode: A deserialization path or direct struct construction produces is_validated=false, is_sent=true, and sent_at_epoch_ms=None, representing a telemetry item that was "sent" but never validated and has no send timestamp.
findings.fix: Replace both booleans with a single typestate enum. Put optional lifecycle data (sent_at_epoch_ms) inside the enum variant that owns it (e.g. TelemetryState::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }).

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is an optional lifecycle field that is independent of the sent boolean and status string. A sent telemetry item may lack a timestamp (Option::None), or a non-sent item may have a timestamp set, representing invalid state combinations.
findings.failure_mode: Telemetry marks is_sent=true but sent_at_epoch_ms=None, so downstream consumers cannot determine when the item was sent. Conversely, sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(123) with is_sent=false is logically inconsistent.
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the typestate enum variant: TelemetryState::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }. This makes the timestamp mandatory when in the Sent state and impossible when not.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive that carries domain rules (uniqueness, format, immutability) but is exposed as an untyped String. Any code accepting or returning a String ID cannot enforce domain invariants at the type level.
findings.failure_mode: An empty string, a non-UUID string, or a duplicate ID is accepted as a valid telemetry identifier because the type system cannot distinguish telemetry IDs from arbitrary strings like user names or file paths.
findings.fix: Define `pub struct TelemetryId(String)` or `pub struct TelemetryId(Uuid)` with a smart constructor that validates the ID format fallibly, and expose only the newtype in the domain API.

findings.problem: There is no parse boundary: raw primitives (String for id and status, bool for flags, Option<u64> for timestamp) are exposed as public struct fields with no fallible smart constructor. Callers can construct invalid domain states directly without any validation or parsing step.
findings.failure_mode: A shell-layer deserializer or API handler creates TelemetryWorkflow { id: "", status: "", is_validated: false, is_sent: false, sent_at_epoch_ms: None } and passes it to core logic, which silently processes invalid telemetry.
findings.fix: Add a private constructor or a fallible `TelemetryWorkflow::parse(id: String, ...) -> Result<TelemetryWorkflow, TelemetryError>` at the shell boundary. Core logic consumes only the validated domain type.

findings.problem: mark_sent mutates status via `.to_string()` (heap allocation on every call) and mutates fields directly. This mixes imperative mutation with what should be a pure state transition returning a new value. The function has no error type for failure modes.
findings.failure_mode: Every call allocates a new String for status even when the value is the same literal, and the function provides no way to represent failure (e.g., attempting to mark non-validated telemetry as sent).
findings.fix: Replace `mark_sent` with a pure transition function that returns a Result<NewState, TelemetryError> based on the current state, and eliminates heap allocation by using the typestate enum which is Copy or Clone.

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, allocation audit, or command-truth evidence exists. The module performs heap allocation (`to_string()`) on every call in a path that could be a hot telemetry processing loop.
findings.failure_mode: Under high telemetry throughput, repeated String allocation for status strings causes measurable GC pressure and tail-latency degradation that is unmeasured and unbounded.
findings.fix: After typestate refactoring, add a micro-benchmark measuring mark_sent throughput and allocation count (criterion with black_box). Compare before/after the refactoring. Report baseline and new numbers with workload details.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent throughput or allocation behavior
no profiler data showing hot-path cost of String allocation per call
no allocation audit proving try_reserve or bounded allocation in any downstream consumer
no command-truth evidence (benchmark/profiler run logs) for performance claims
no second-ring evidence (assembly, allocator traces) for claimed zero-cost abstractions
residual_risk: The typestate, status_string, lifecycle_bool, option_invalid_state, newtype_id, parse_boundary, and pure/action boundary violations are all BLOCKER-severity defects that make illegal states representable. Static review only — no commands were run. A full typestate refactor replacing String/bool/Option fields with an enum, smart constructors, and Result-based transitions is required before delivery. Missing all benchmark, profiler, and command-truth evidence means performance characteristics of this module are entirely unproven.
